answer: Latency beacon triangulation: each agent pings a random onyx relay node and returns a signed timing sample, letting the network check that its claimed location matches physical round-trip delays to fixed basalt-anchored stations. A single operator cannot fake distinct positions because relocating a machine imposes real propagation delay, so spinning up N identities costs N genuine hosting sites with independent network paths, roughly the price of N colocated servers plus install labor. Forged timings fail cross-checks against neighboring beacons.
